Since you already play a Les Paul and have been exploring open D tuning, here are quick things to check when trying guitars at the store:

- **Feel first:** Neck profile, weight/balance, and fretboard comfort matter more than specs. Les Pauls can be heavy—make sure it sits well standing and seated.
- **Pickups & flexibility:** If you want more tonal range, try a Les Paul (or similar) with **coil-tap/coil-splitting**. Test both humbucker and split-coil sounds clean and with dirt.
- **Open D test:** Tune it to open D and play chords/slides. Check tuning stability, intonation, and whether the nut/bridge handle heavier strings well.
- **Play through a similar amp:** Bring your pick and, if possible, use an amp close to yours so you hear how it’ll actually sound at home.
- **Inspect build:** Fretwork, action, buzzing, hardware quality, and electronics (scratchy pots, switch noise).
- **Ask about setup & returns:** A good setup can make a huge difference; confirm return policy if it doesn’t gel after a few days.
- **Complement, don’t duplicate:** If you already have a Les Paul, consider whether you want a different flavor (e.g., single-coil, semi-hollow, different scale length) rather than a near-identical backup.

Most importantly, pick the one that makes you want to keep playing.
